title: Replacing Illinois Jacquet; who played tenor and alto
summary: Cobb replaced Jacquet in Hampton's band and says Jacquet was an alto player whom Hampton put on tenor in 1940.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Were you two ever in the band together?
Illinois and I?
: Yeah.
Right here in Houston. With Milt Larkin's band.
: No, no -- I mean with Lionel.
No. he was on Lionel's band when I got there.
: But he quit?
I took his place. HE DIDN'T QUIT. duet with, do the
: Well, but whom did you do the act with?
Johnny Griffin. That was my son. Johnny Griffin He was the little ...
: Yeah, but who did Jack do it with, Jacquet who did Illinois do it with?
I wasn't there ... I don't know. I don't know.
: Did you originate that "Flyin' Home" thing?

Right here in Houston, and he got it on record before me. But it wasn't "Flying Home" -- it was another tune we played here, and I played it. See, I was the tenor saxophone player -- and he was an alto player. Hampton put him on tenor.
: Who did?
Lionel Hampton.
: Oh, he did?
In 1940. See, Illinois Jacquet was an alto saxophone player.
Well, when he was with Milt, he played alto?
Alto. No tenor. I'm the tenor player. Tom Archer was a tenor player. Illinois was a saxophone player ... alto. Hamp put him on tenor. Okay, I'm telling you what the story is. If I'm lying, you're ...
So then did he pick up your style then?
He picked up everything!
He didn't ... I mean on alto ...
